value.name: compares conflicting document numbers
value.description: Asha notices the mismatch between the clerk's inked stamp and her own trial-pad notation and recognizes she cannot dispute the discrepancy.
evidence: r-eighteen sat in the clerk's ink in the upper right corner of the intake page, and her own hand had written five-oh-six in the trial pad two inches away, and the gap between the two numbers was not a thing she could argue with once she had put them on the same surface.

value.name: Devin observes silently
value.description: Devin watches Asha examine the documents without leaving the counter or interrupting her.
evidence: Devin watched her do it without moving from the counter

value.name: Asha closes and packs the records
value.description: Asha shuts the pad over the log, returns both documents to the briefcase, and secures it.
evidence: she closed the pad over the log, slid both back into the briefcase, and snapped the latch

value.name: Asha decides to bring evidence to Whitfield
value.description: Asha tells Devin she is taking the documents to Whitfield before one o'clock, revealing both resolve and discomfort.
evidence: "I'm going to Whitfield with this before one," she said, and the sentence cost her less than she had expected and more than she wanted Devin to see.

value.name: Asha leaves the apartment with documents
value.description: Asha exits the apartment carrying the briefcase and rehearsing how she will explain the mistake to Whitfield.
evidence: She let herself out of the apartment with the documents under her arm

by the time she reached the elevator she was already rehearsing the first plain sentence she would put in front of Whitfield, which was that the stamp was four-eighteen and that she had been wrong about the order.

value.name: Asha arrives at Whitfield's office
value.description: Asha comes down the firm's back corridor and stops at Whitfield's door, preparing herself before entering.
evidence: Asha came up the firm's back corridor with the briefcase against her hip and stopped at Whitfield's door without knocking yet.
She tightened her grip on the handles, took one slow breath through her nose, and let the sentence she had rehearsed in the elevator settle into the order she wanted it in.

value.name: Asha presents the records to Whitfield
value.description: Asha enters Whitfield's office, places the briefcase on a chair, and lays out the trial record and intake log so the conflicting stamps are visible together.
evidence: Whitfield looked up from his desk when she came through; she set the briefcase on the near chair, unlatched it, and laid the Hatcher trial record and the clerk's intake log on his blotter so the four-eighteen stamp sat above her own five-oh-six in the same line of sight.

value.name: Asha states the stamp discrepancy
value.description: Asha begins her explanation to Whitfield by stating that the stamp is four-eighteen.
